scope: Posthoc descriptive audit of archived development data; no new fitting, inference, confirmation, or attention intervention.

definitions.attention: Current-query K3 content softmax, not future-attention training labels.
definitions.K2_weights: Algebraic K3-weight renormalization over the retained pair; logits are itemwise and unchanged. Mean over both items is trivially 0.5 and is not evidence of uniform attention.
definitions.single: One candidate plus current blank at fixed ages [6,4]; known-axis bit is extracted from the nearest full-outcome prototype. It is not joint future accuracy; D decoy is excluded.
definitions.oracle: argmin expected MSE across 32 evaluation plans. Diagnostic classes below use the distinct actual episode plan.
definitions.confidence: Prototype-distance margins are geometric scores, not calibrated confidence. Closeness to the prototype mean does not establish an uncertainty mechanism.
definitions.K2: Accuracy tables distinguish native and fixed ages rather than pooling them.

general_mean_pooling_counterexample.nonlinear_decoder: recover counts; find tag with count two; parity of its bit-one count
general_mean_pooling_counterexample.scope: Existence example only; not a claim that archived DINO/projection or learned decoder realizes it.

interpretation_limits: Strong tag-dependent attention and K3 error associations support a reader bottleneck hypothesis, not proof that softmax alone causes all errors.
Adding the third item changes several reader channels together. It is a saved subset intervention, not an isolated attention-weight intervention.
The independent scalar eviction bound does not apply to a nonlinear decoder operating on an aggregated set representation.
K2 equal weights hold for identical local observations; different payload and/or salient styling can yield unequal weights.
Oracle semantic disagreement can coexist with correct nearest-prototype classification. Do not equate all 159 cases with confidently wrong complete predictions or midpoint hedging.
